summary: A GeoPackage or shapefile ZIP cannot reach parts and a package through the batch's large path
without changing seams outside SH1's owned paths. Per the task file, the work stopped and the
seams are named here; no code was written.

why: Returns null unless item.card.format is 'geojson' and the source is large-original-v1, so no
large step job is ever queued for a GeoPackage or shapefile ZIP item. The task file marks this
The reader is always enqueued with framing 'feature-collection'; the part carries readerVersion
'geojson-stream/2'; each packaged feature is sliced from the original by its GeoJSON byte range.
A GeoPackage row or a .dbf record has no such span. Not an owned path.
A package proves each feature by re-parsing its raw GeoJSON bytes (SourceRangeReference format
'geojson'). A native record needs a decoded-record proof (re-read by row id or record position,
as CB1 cites it). Not an owned path.
The reader opens one object stream and parses GeoJSON or a workbook; it has no native GIS
framing, refuses a large original that is not octet-stream JSON bytes, and writes the streamed-
map receipt only for 'feature-collection'. Not an owned path.
Parts, profile and mapping records require GeoJSON byte locators; a native window needs a record
locator (layer, row id or record position) instead. Not an owned path.
The native reader takes the whole original as base64 of at most 16 MiB and reads at most 2,000
features in one call. A windowed read (keyset by row id, about 1,000 a window) needs the
original on scratch disk or read from object storage, as point_batch.py and projected_vector.py
do. This part is owned, but without the seams above it would be unwired code.

proposedSplit: One owner for the large-path seam: a native-GIS framing in contracts and the streaming reader,
records located by layer and row id or record position, a decoded-record part proof beside the
GeoJSON byte proof, and largeStateKey and the worker accepting a GeoPackage or shapefile-ZIP
Then SH1 as written: the windowed native reader in native_gis.py, the intake-draft recipe for
these cards, and the tests (more than 2,000 polygons through the batch, a shapefile ZIP, a two-
layer GeoPackage, a layer with no CRS).
